transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Mei Chen (Redwood SE), Omar Nash (Redwood Partner Lead); Aisha Khan (Cumulus Head of Cloud Partnerships), Ben Turner (VP Infra), Dr. Max Li (ML Systems), Sofia Rios (TPM)

Summary:
Introductory partner discovery to scope a GPU onramp integration between Redwood Inference and Cumulus Labs. Focus areas: private connectivity options (VPC vs. direct), capacity billing model, certificate/KMS integration, benchmark plan and early pilot scope. Agreement to run a short perf check on a 7B model and follow up with a technical deep dive and security review.

Topics covered:
- Cumulus infra topology and multi-tenant cluster model
- Network patterns: VPC peering, private link, and SASE considerations
- Data residency and encryption/KMS integration options
- Billing and reserved capacity vs. burst routing (Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted)
- Benchmarking plan and success criteria for pilot

Action items (captured):
- Jordan to send partner one-pager, SSO/SSO sample config, and link to integration brief by 2026-09-17
- Mei to draft benchmark plan + sample dataset and runbook by 2026-09-19
- Aisha to confirm cluster access approach and security contacts by 2026-09-20

Transcript body (timestamps rough, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, happy to kick off, uh, brief intros then we'll go into what Cumulus is seeing on their side.
[00:18] Aisha: Thanks Jordan, yeah, hi all, Aisha here, I'll hand over to Ben to run through our infra, but quick note: we are looking for a partner to help us onboard customers with high-throughput LLM workloads and, you know, keep unit cost predictable.
[00:34] Ben: hi, Ben Turner, VP infra. Quick topo: we run a hybrid fleet, mostly AWS bare-metal in a few regions and a private colo cluster in EU-west for regulated clients. We have a tenant model — logical tenants on shared GPU nodes — and we use a controller that we built, called cloudlet (not public), to schedule.
[00:55] Mei: ok that's helpful — do you shard tenants by node groups or by pods?
[01:03] Ben: It's a mix, node-group isolation for high-trust customers, otherwise shared. Our questions today are around how Redwood would route requests: dedicated capacity vs hosted fallback, and how the billing would look if we front Redwood capacity from our infra.
[01:20] Jordan: Right, so two common patterns: 1) Redwood Dedicated where you reserve capacity we manage and it's isolated, or 2) Onramp model where Redwood runtime can be deployed into partner infra and we do smart routing. In the second case, billing is typically usage based with an overlay for reserved units — a hybrid.
[01:40] Dr. Max Li: quick clarification — when you say "deploy into partner infra" is that the private control plane or the full on-prem package? We have some air-gapped customers.
[01:51] Omar: good question. We offer a private deployment (VPC/on-prem) where the control plane can be customer-managed; for air-gapped we have an on-prem bundle. There's also a VPC peering flow for lower friction.
[02:08] Sofia: are the KMS/HSM integrations supported, like bringing our keys?
[02:13] Mei: yes, we support customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, and we emit audit logs for inference requests. There may be some upstream compliance work but it's standard for our Private offering.
[02:26] Ben: Another practical: we need to see latency numbers. Our target is 50–120 ms p95 for small chat completions for a 7B model in EU. How are you measuring that?
[02:36] Jordan: We'll propose a benchmark plan — headroom for batching, KV cache reuse, and expected network egress. Mei will own the benchmark details.
[02:46] Mei: I can do a short benchmark: 7B model, a mix of short prompts (avg 32 tokens) and medium chat sequences (avg 120 tokens). We'll instrument token-level latency, p50/p95/p99, and token cost.
[02:59] Aisha: Great. Also, governance: our compliance team will need SOC2-type docs, plus a data retention policy. Do you have a standard pack?
[03:08] Jordan: yes we'll share SOC2 artifacts and a partner security pack. Omar: and we can add RBAC examples and sample audit logs.
[03:18] Ben: Ok, on networking: our preference is VPC endpoint (private link style) over opening public endpoints. Can Redwood support strictly private endpoints?
[03:28] Mei: yes, private link, VPC peering, and direct connect are supported patterns. One note: if you want the lowest latency we often recommend co-locating the runtime on the same network fabric — that tends to reduce token latency by 10–30ms depending on rack locality.
[03:44] Dr. Max Li: about KV cache — we've built an LRU cache in our scheduling layer, but I'm worried about correctness when routing requests across multiple replicas. How does Redwood manage KV cache consistency?
[03:58] Mei: great question. Our runtime shards KV cache per-request context and supports warm KV sharing between replicas via a prefix-cache sync; it's not perfect but for short convo state it's usually fine. Note the transcript might say "K V cash" elsewhere, but it's KV cache.
[04:18] Ben: caveat — we do eviction aggressively, so we need to see cache hit rates to evaluate cost benefits.
[04:26] Jordan: noted, we'll surface cache metrics in the dashboards.
[04:32] Sofia: one of our partners is asking about model variants — do you do fallbacks if a particular model isn't hosted in a region?
[04:40] Omar: Yes, smart routing: the platform can fallback to compatible model variants or route to a hosted pool. You can configure policy — prefer same-region low-latency, or prefer cheapest.
[04:52] Ben: are there hard SLOs for fallback? We need predictable behavior for customer SLAs.
[04:57] Jordan: For Dedicated we can contract SLOs. For onramp integrated setups we'll recommend canary policies and automatic fallback thresholds; SLA discussion is part of later enterprise contracting.
[05:10] Aisha: timeline — we want a pilot by end of Q4. Is that realistic?
[05:16] Mei: yes, pilot in 6–8 weeks depending on cluster access and dataset prep. The critical path is credentials and bench harness access.
[05:25] Dr. Max Li: about data residency: some regulated customers require logs to stay in-country. Can we gate where logs live?
[05:33] Omar: yes, we can configure log retention regionally; for Private we leave logs in customer-controlled storage. We'll need to map retention rules though.
[05:44] Ben: cost model — for the onramp, do you charge per-token or per-commit for reserved capacity?
[05:50] Jordan: we typically combine both: a reserved base (monthly commit for Dedicated pools) plus a usage overlay. For partner-managed infra we can do flat per-hour runtime cost + token usage, or negotiate a channel rate. We can provide a sample pricing sheet.
[06:05] Aisha: can you support reseller billing? Our sales ops expect consolidated invoices.
[06:10] Omar: yes, reseller billing and marketplace options are supported; we often integrate via partner marketplaces or direct invoicing.
[06:18] Ben: security review — we'll need to schedule a formal run with our security team. Any special items we should expect?
[06:24] Mei: expect checks around KMS key handling, network architecture, audit logs, and third-party dependency lists. We can share a standard security questionnaire.
[06:33] Jordan: Action: I'll send the security pack and SOC2 evidence.
[06:38] Aisha: Great. A few nitty-gritty questions from our infra folks: what GPU flavors do you optimize for? A lot of our nodes are A100, a handful are H100 — we also have some older T4s in dev.
[06:51] Mei: runtime supports A100 and H100 optimizations, and we do quantized paths for T4-like devices but with different perf profiles. We'll include a perf matrix.
[07:02] Dr. Max Li: how do you handle model compilation and kernel selection? we have a mixed-precision policy.
[07:08] Mei: the runtime auto-selects kernels based on architecture and sequence-length distribution; for special precision needs we can pin kernel sets per-route. There will be a small compile step for model variants.
[07:20] Ben: ok. Real-world test — we want you to run a 7B chat workload with 8 concurrent sessions per node, see p95 and token cost. Can Redwood provide a harness we can run on our cluster?
[07:32] Jordan: Yes — we can ship a lightweight runner and a runbook. Mei will share the harness repo link and run instructions.
[07:39] Sofia: will you need service account keys, or can you do ephemeral access?
[07:43] Mei: ephemeral credentials via short-lived certs are preferred for tests; we support that.
[07:48] Aisha: compliance again — for the pilot customers we will need data deletion guarantees and proof of deletion.
[07:55] Omar: for Private deployments we can enable customer-controlled storage and deletion hooks; we'll provide delete logs as part of the audit trail.
[08:05] Ben: any blockers you foresee?
[08:08] Mei: biggest friction is access to a test cluster and agreement on model weight access (some internal models are licensed). If you can host an open-source 7B model for the first run that removes licensing friction.
[08:21] Aisha: yes we'll prefer OSS weights for benching. We'll confirm which 7B to use.
[08:27] Jordan: summary of next steps: Jordan sends partner brief + SSO and security pack; Mei shares bench harness and drafts plan; Aisha confirms cluster access and compliance contacts. Everyone agreed?
[08:40] Aisha: yep.
[08:42] Ben: yep.
[08:43] Dr. Max Li: yep.
[08:44] Jordan: excellent, we'll target the dates we discussed. Thanks all.
[08:50] (meeting wraps, small crosstalk)

Notes/Minor transcription artifacts: speakers sometimes overlapped, proper nouns like "cloudlet" were auto-corrected to "cloud let" in places; "KV cache" may appear as "K V cash" in some auto-text.
